annotations.keyFindings: Fourteen readiness tools, mostly self-report skill checklists; content validity adequate for eight, predictive validity tested for three, none across conditions.
annotations.limitations: Measurement review only; few tools tested in intellectual disability or other languages.

annotations.keyFindings: Readiness at 17 did not predict HbA1c or attendance 12 months after transfer; meeting a named adult clinician did.
annotations.limitations: One condition; one region; attendance only up to 12 months.

annotations.keyFindings: Young people felt questionnaires tested knowledge they already had; readiness was described as confidence within relationships; low scores delayed transfer against wishes.
annotations.limitations: Two clinics; conversations led by clinic staff.

annotations.keyFindings: A structured programme with joint clinics and a coordinator raised first adult appointment attendance from 64 to 82 percent.
Ceiling effects from 16 onward (38 percent of 17-year-olds at the ceiling) and condition-dependent medication items.
Lower readiness scores were associated with lower health literacy and deprivation; interpreter users scored lowest with an English-only questionnaire.
An adapted pictorial version with supported completion worked for 40 of 44 adolescents with intellectual disability.
annotations.limitations: Small; no reliability or predictive testing.

annotations.keyFindings: Readiness-based transfer came nine months later than age-based transfer without better one-year outcomes, and young people were more frustrated.
annotations.limitations: Two clinics differing in staffing and joint clinics.

synthesis: Eight retrieved records, appraised at abstract level after a first reply arrived as markdown and was not applied. Readiness tools mostly measure knowledge and self-management skills, and few have been tested for prediction. In the one prospective study, readiness at 17 did not predict outcomes after transfer, while meeting a named adult clinician did. Young people and parents describe readiness as confidence within relationships, scores show ceiling effects and track health literacy and deprivation, and adapted versions are needed for intellectual disability. Structured programmes improve attendance, but their readiness component cannot be separated from joint clinics.
gradeRationale: One measurement review of moderate quality and otherwise single-site observational and qualitative studies; consistent in suggesting that scores should not gate transfer, but indirect across conditions.
summary: Eight retrieved records appraised; four source-derived claims; overall certainty low.
